verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.6 'Main-thread work' (the section heading is [D]; the sentence itself has no qualifier): 'No engine call on the main thread may become a long task (50 ms) on that phone. The rule of E-9 is sized for this'. This supports the finding's expected value, with the caveat on per-call versus per-task in the reason. decisions/P5-A2.md 'where each call runs': 'A pick builds the representation one engine call per task'. decisions/P5-A2.md 'hydration (review finding 4, request 10)': 'hydration computes the facts of the node only ... no relation list, move matrix, signed move or grid is computed or drawn in the hydration task'. DECISIONS.md 'MERGE: P5 stages 5.2 and 5.3 repaired after review': the held item is limited to 'minusculeMatrices on the B8, C8 and D8 nodes of 1120 and 1792 positions'.
verdicts.evidence: Read at 006f50d: SPEC 7.6 whole, 5.1 E-9 and E-11, 7.4, the T12 heading (phase 5) and 9.1 row 5 (G5). Also read DECISIONS.md, decisions/P5-A2.md, reports/gate-G5.md (gate commit line names 006f50d), the phase 5 review and repair JSONs, the phase 4 RT-07 output, RT-07 lens attacks 22 and 24 and its section 6, and P5-LENS-INSTRUCTIONS 'Known and decided'. Code at 006f50d confirms the cause. model.ts:575: admitLink validates with new T12Tool(configOf(state), {defer: true, need: 'staged'}). model.ts:211-213: in the browser, 'staged' runs addMatrices (minusculeMatrices) and addSignedMoves for every node synchronously. T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:600-604: the hydration $effect calls readLink, which calls admitLink and then load(), which builds T12Tool again with 'staged'. build() (:520-545) instead runs representationSteps (model.ts:150-176), one engine call per task and one task per node above 300 positions. model.ts:186 documents 'staged' as 'a state loaded after hydration', but readLink runs inside hydration. T12.spec.ts:907 tests long tasks only for picks. On the two held items: (1) the E-9 sizing the owner holds covers 1120 and 1792 positions (B8, C8, D8 nodes 4 and 5) and the size of one call. The finding's nodes have 240 to 1024 positions (E8:8, D8:3, E6:4, D7:5, E7:6, B8:7, C8:7). Its controls isolate grouping as the cause: picks of the same nodes have no long task at 1x, and links to small orbits have none. (2) The lab acceptance concerns Lighthouse TBT figures in the G3 range. This finding compares per-task measurements against pick and small-orbit controls on the same machine, not a lab figure. Strongest counter-record: DECISIONS.md 'RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf: what the residual of P3-RT-07-02 was' ('SPEC 7.6 ... says only that no engine call ... may become a long task; it does not say how a tool's load should be shaped when hydration itself is long') and 'MERGE: red-team round 1, residual fixes' ('The load is still one long task ... which is Svelte's hydration and render ..., not engine work; SPEC 7.6 bounds engine calls'). Those records accepted a long task only because it was not engine work, with about 30 ms of engine work in it. Their board-load.spec entry treats 'no task's share of engine work reaches 50 ms' as the property checked. Here the extra task time is the engine work that the link path groups.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: the cause is neither held item (it is not the owner's E-9 sizing of minusculeMatrices on the 1120- and 1792-position orbits, and not the machine-bound lab TBT) but a link load that runs in the hydration task what a pick splits into one engine call per task. R1 fails: no sentence of 7.6, 7.4 or E-9 permits grouping engine calls into one long hydration task, and the P3 residual record accepted a long load task only because it was Svelte work, not engine work. R2 fails: the finding quotes 7.6 correctly, but there is a real ambiguity for the owner. 7.6 literally bounds 'an engine call', and at 1x the finding's largest single call (minusculeMatrices on C8 node 7, 34.5 ms sampled with profiler overhead) is under 50 ms. The project's own records, though (P5-A2 pick split and 'hydration computes the facts only'; the P3 residual 'task's share of engine work'), read the bound per task. R3 fails: T12 is phase 5 at gate G5. R4 fails: the oracle has nothing on timing. R5 fails: 7.6 is [D], but no record makes a link load an exception; P5-A2's hydration record says the opposite. R6 fails: there is no record in gate-G5.md, the phase 5 reviews or earlier rounds. Major fits 'a behaviour the specification states is missing or wrong'.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 5.6, last sentence (unlabelled; 5.6 has no [D]): 'A tool decides whether a board is of finite type by calling `classify` once when the board is loaded, never by running an enumeration into its cap.' SPEC.md 5.1 E-11: the verdict is kept in a WeakMap keyed by board object. This supports the finding's expected value.
verdicts.evidence: Read 5.6 whole and E-11 at 006f50d. The 5.6 sentence has no 'may' or 'unless'. The finding's quote drops the closing clause 'never by running an enumeration into its cap', which does not change the 'once'. The records read 'once' as a count per load. decisions/P2-A7.md 'the verdict cache in state.ts': resolveBoard 'calls classify once' (reason SPEC 5.6). site/src/lib/state.ts:220-228 (the resolvedThisRun comment): 'A tool loads its board in one such run ... one classify per load. The map is emptied in a microtask'. P3-RT-07-02 was confirmed on this reading in round 1 and fixed (DECISIONS.md 'MERGE: red-team round 1, group B': 'one classify per load'). Code: a T12 pick is spread over tasks by design (decisions/P5-A2.md, 'A pick builds the representation one engine call per task'). In those tasks resolveBoard runs at T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:534 (defaultNode(resolveBoard(spec))), model.ts:157 or :200 (startRepresentation(resolveBoard(spec))) and model.ts:409 (the T12Tool constructor in load()). resolvedThisRun is cleared at the next microtask (state.ts:265), so each task builds a new object and verdictOf classifies it. Nothing at 006f50d records an exception for multi-task loads: P5-A2.md mentions resolveBoard only as part of the hydration cost. state-classify-once.test.ts has no T12 case, and T12.test.ts and T12.spec.ts do not count classify.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails, because 5.6 has no qualifier allowing more than one classify per load. R2 fails, because a board pick is a board load and the project's records (P2-A7, the resolvedThisRun comment, the confirmed P3-RT-07-02) read 'once' as a count. R3 fails: T12 is phase 5 at G5 and 5.6 applies from phase 2. R4 fails: this is not a mathematical value. R5 fails: 5.6 is not [D], and P5-A2 records the pick split but not repeated classification. R6 fails: there is no open record, and no regression test covers T12. Severity stays as claimed: the rubric is silent on a repeated internal computation that has no observable effect, and the lens's attack 24 rates this case minor.
